Template drift within one district, eight weeks apart.

quote: How to manage the direct filing of new actions in the MDL proceedings; … Any actions later filed in, removed to, or transferred to this Court will be consolidated automatically with this action, without the need for a motion or entry of an order by the Court. … any plaintiff whose case would be subject to transfer to MDL No. 3170 may file their case directly in the United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, noting on the civil cover sheet that the case is related to Case Number 25 CV 10320 and MDL No. 3170. All plaintiffs directly filing in the U.S. District Court, Northern District of Illinois, are required to pay the standard New Action Filing Fee to initiate the case.
coding_note: THE ONLY EXPRESS DIRECT-FILING PERMISSION IN THE CODED SET. Every other order that resolves this subject does so passively, by providing that actions later filed in the district are automatically consolidated. CMO #1 ¶ 6 does the opposite: it affirmatively invites plaintiffs whose cases would be subject to transfer to file directly in this district, states the reason ('To eliminate delays associated with transfer of cases filed in or removed from other federal district courts'), and prescribes the mechanics, a civil cover sheet notation and payment of the standard filing fee. Rule 16.1(b)(2)(D) asks the parties how to manage direct filing; this court answered the question itself, in a companion order, on the same day it asked it.

The language closely tracks the Manual for Complex Litigation, Fourth, § 10.221, which matters because ¶ 1.e directs counsel to be familiar with the Manual and the order never cites Rule 16.1.

Adjacent language considered and rejected under application rule R3: ¶ 4.a describes Lead Counsel formulating positions 'in consultation with other counsel' and 'presenting written and oral arguments and suggestions to the court,' but that paragraph is about the role's functions, not about establishing methods for regularly communicating with and reporting to the court and nonleadership counsel. ¶ 1.a's 'frequency of regular status conferences' is coded at b2c_conference_schedule.

Two adjacent provisions considered and rejected. ¶ 4.a's 'Plaintiffs' Lead Counsel will act for the group' concentrates functions in lead counsel but does not raise limits on nonleadership activity as a subject. ¶ 1.b's permission for parties with similar interests to agree on a single attorney at the conference is a voluntary economy, treated the same way as MDL 3166 ¶ 11 and MDL 3171 ¶ 12.

quote: Attorney fee proposals, rates, and/or percentages that applicants expect to seek if the litigation succeeds in creating a common fund. The Court observes that it shall make the final determination as to the compensation and reimbursement of Plaintiffs' Counsel.
coding_note: THE ONLY ORDER IN THE SET THAT MAKES FEE EXPECTATIONS PART OF THE LEADERSHIP APPLICATION. Partial resolution: no compensation means is established, but two things are fixed that no report can alter. Applicants must disclose expected rates and percentages at the application stage, and the court reserves the final determination on compensation and reimbursement to itself. Compare MDL 3163 Part IV.B.4, which raises a common benefit fund as a topic and fixes nothing, and MDL 3171 ¶ 8, which asks applicants to discuss a common benefit fund approach in a case plan.

quote: Orders of Transferor Courts. All orders by transferor courts imposing dates for pleading or discovery are vacated.
coding_note: RESOLVED but not DIRECTED. The strongest treatment of (b)(2)(B) in the set, and it completes a three-way contrast on one subject. MDLs 3162, 3166, and 3171 CONTINUE transferor-court orders in force until modified; MDL 3185 STAYS the deadlines they imposed; this order VACATES them outright. Nothing is asked of the parties about prior orders anywhere in the report content at ¶ 5.b, so party_direction is FALSE.

quote: The Court intends to address the following issues at the initial scheduling conference: … (4) preliminary case management issues, including the frequency of regular status conferences,
coding_note: IDENTIFIED under application rule R4: this is what the Court intends to address, and no item in the mandatory report content at ¶ 5.b covers conference scheduling. Nothing beyond the August 5 conference is set.

quote: Later Filed Cases. This Order shall also apply to related cases later filed in, removed to, or transferred to this Court. … A statement of counsel's view(s) on best practices for docket management in light of the estimated total number of cases (i.e., whether documents affecting all actions be filed only on the MDL docket, or also on the dockets of the individual actions).
coding_note: Both attributes. ¶ 6.f fixes automatic application of this order to later-filed cases and ¶ 6.b.ii fixes the master-file filing rule, neither of which the report can change. What remains open, and is directed, is the docket-management practice for filings across member cases.

quote: A list of all known related cases pending in state or federal court and their current status. … An estimate of the total number of related cases counsel expect to be filed.
coding_note: Partial resolution on the same basis as MDLs 3163 and 3166: coordination methods are left open, but the court fixes how related-action information is gathered, in a single joint report of no more than twenty-five pages, prepared by defendants' counsel, due July 24. ¶ 1.c separately invites parties in related federal and state litigation to attend the conference, which no other order in the set does.

quote: A statement of counsel's position(s) on the need for consolidated and/or master complaint(s), and/or short-form complaint(s) in this action.
coding_note: Three pleading forms named where the Rule names one: consolidated, master, and short-form complaints. Short-form complaints are a products-liability mechanism the Rule does not mention. Nothing is fixed.

Not raised, which is notable in a products liability MDL. No census, no plaintiff fact sheet, no initial-disclosures reference. ¶ 5.b.vii asks for a list of outstanding discovery, which is discovery status and is coded at b3c_discovery.

quote: A list of all outstanding discovery. … Pending further order of this Court, all outstanding discovery proceedings are stayed, and no further discovery shall be initiated.
coding_note: Both attributes. The stay is reinforced by ¶ 6.c, which vacates transferor-court orders imposing discovery dates, so the existing discovery calendar is not merely paused but removed. The Rule's 'difficult issues' language does not appear.

quote: A statement of counsel's position(s) on how the Court should address the pending motions to dismiss in the individual cases. … Except for motions for emergency relief, no motion shall be filed until and in accordance with the Scheduling Order. All pending motions must be renoticed for resolution once the Court sets a schedule for any such motions.
coding_note: The strongest motion-practice restriction in the set: a general prohibition on filing any motion except for emergency relief until the Scheduling Order issues, plus mandatory renoticing, plus an extension of defendants' time to respond. Resolution under application rule R2 several times over. The report must separately list pending motions, adjudicated motions, and positions on the outstanding motions to dismiss.
Not raised. No settlement, mediation, ADR, or settlement master reference anywhere in the order. ¶ 5.b.ix concerns a Rule 53 special master and is coded at b3f_magistrate_master.

quote: Counsel's position(s) on whether there is a need to appoint a special master pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 53 or an independent scientific expert.
coding_note: Half of (b)(3)(F). The order asks about a special master, cites Rule 53 by number, and adds an independent scientific expert, which the Rule does not mention. It never asks about referral to a magistrate judge, even though the case is assigned to one. No appointment is made.

quote: A statement of counsel's understanding of the facts and the key legal issues in this case. Counsel should underscore where facts and legal issues may materially differ between certain categories of cases. Any potentially dispositive issues should be separately identified.
coding_note: Richer than the Rule's item in two ways: it asks counsel to differentiate issues across categories of cases, and to flag potentially dispositive issues separately. 'Key legal issues' rather than the Rule's 'principal factual and legal issues.'

pin_cite: p.1 (in-person requirement); p.1 topic 1; p.2 (FURTHER ORDERED)
quote: Counsel applying for leadership shall appear in person. … Plaintiffs’ counsel’s proposed leadership structure and related applications; … IT IS FURTHER ORDERED that, to the extent the parties do not reach consensus on the appointment of the plaintiffs’ lead counsel, steering committee, or liaison counsel, applications for such appointments shall be filed by June 23, 2026.
coding_note: Conditional resolution, codebook test case 4. Consensus among the parties extinguishes the application process; failure to agree triggers applications due June 23. Either branch is set by the order rather than choosable by the parties' status reports. Plaintiffs' side only.

quote: applications for such appointments shall be filed by June 23, 2026.
coding_note: Express by description rather than by the Rule's label, and only partially: the order fixes the front end of the appointment timetable, the application deadline, but unlike MDLs 3166 and 3171 it says nothing about when the court will appoint. Twelve days from order to application deadline, and three days from that deadline to the conference.

quote: Plaintiffs’ counsel’s proposed leadership structure and related applications; … the appointment of the plaintiffs’ lead counsel, steering committee, or liaison counsel,
coding_note: Three roles are named as possible appointments, but the structure is expressly the parties' to propose, so nothing is fixed.

quote: Applications should be filed using the ECF event “Request (Not to be Used as a Motion)” found under Civil Events, Other Filings, Other Documents. … Counsel applying for leadership shall appear in person.
coding_note: The thinnest prescribed selection procedure in the set that still counts as resolution: a condition, a deadline, a specified docket event, and an in-person appearance requirement, with no criteria, no page limits, and no objection window. Contrast MDLs 3166, 3171, and 3181, where the criteria and format are prescribed in detail.

quote: Notable orders entered by any transferor court prior to consolidation; … All deadlines in all consolidated cases, including deadlines imposed by order of a transferor court, are STAYED pending further order of this Court.
coding_note: RESOLUTION BY DISPLACEMENT, and the mirror image of the continuation provisions elsewhere in the set. MDLs 3162, 3166, and 3171 leave transferor-court orders in full force until modified; this order stays the deadlines those orders imposed. Both are operative determinations, in opposite directions. Entered on a defendants' consent motion (Doc. 4), which is the only granted motion in any coded order.

quote: The scheduling of a Rule 16 conference, if necessary, and subsequent regular status conferences; and
coding_note: Express treatment of (b)(2)(C), but note the citation: this order refers to 'a Rule 16 conference,' not a Rule 16.1 conference, and contains no reference to Rule 16.1 anywhere. Entered June 11, 2026, more than six months after the Rule took effect. Nothing beyond the June 26 initial conference is scheduled.

quote: A proposed schedule for the filing of a consolidated complaint and subsequent case management deadlines, including whether and when mediation should occur;
coding_note: 'Consolidated complaint' rather than the Rule's 'consolidated pleadings.' The schedule is the parties' to propose.

quote: The nature and status of any pending motions filed prior to consolidation; … including any pending or anticipated motions to remand or dismiss, with proposed briefing schedules, … All deadlines in all consolidated cases, including deadlines imposed by order of a transferor court, are STAYED pending further order of this Court.
coding_note: A stronger express treatment of (b)(3)(D) than the Rule's own text: the order names the two anticipated motion types and asks for proposed briefing schedules. Resolution under application rule R2, since the blanket stay fixes when any motion is due.

coding_note: Named measure, mediation, embedded inside the scheduling topic. Nothing is fixed and no mediator or master is identified.

coding_note: Sequencing vocabulary rather than the Rule's identification vocabulary: 'threshold issues that, if resolved early, will significantly advance the litigation,' which matches the 'priority' and 'threshold' framing in MDLs 3166 and 3171 rather than the Rule's 'principal factual and legal issues.'
